page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable performance instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the t3a.xlarge in the lower performance tiers for most compute-intensive tasks. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 10% category, with scores of 566.4 and 1181.97 respectively. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block operations measured at 23.87 GB/sec and write operations at 11.7 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates average performance in the PassMark CPU encryption test with a score of 3207.35, but falls into the bottom 10% for database operations, software compilation, and static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t3a.xlarge offers a budget-friendly hardware profile designed for workloads with variable CPU utilization. Because it utilizes a burstable CPU allocation model, it is suited for applications that remain idle or run at low baseline levels but require occasional bursts of compute power. Suitable workloads include low-traffic web servers, development environments, small code repositories, and basic background tasks that do not require sustained high-performance compute or high-speed local storage.
